notes: ACCESS ROUTE: davidjones.com runs Imperva/Incapsula bot-interstitial on every direct fetch -- homepage returns a fixed 6183-byte 'Pardon Our Interruption' JS-challenge shell (confirmed identical across 16 curl_cffi browser impersonation profiles: chrome99-131, edge99/101, safari15/17, firefox133 -- all blocked identically). r.jina.ai returned HTTP 403. Working route: Google translate.goog proxy (host www-davidjones-com.translate.goog, params _x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=fr&_x_tr_hl=en) -- returns the full server-rendered Next.js HTML with all embedded JSON-LD/category data intact and in English (the translation widget only rewrites visible DOM text client-side; the raw SSR payload we fetch is untouched, confirmed by checking meta/og titles and category names stayed English). robots.txt checked first (Rule 3): no Claude-specific disallow, only standard filter/sort/refine query-param disallows (not used here). COUNT METHOD: each listing page embeds schema.org ItemList JSON-LD with an exact 'numberOfItems' field; exhaustion-verified via pagination boundary check on two categories (Dinnerware: page 43 returns numberOfItems=1013, page 44 returns HTTP 404; Candle Holders: page 6 returns numberOfItems=139, page 7 returns HTTP 404) -- confirms the field is the true exhaustive total, not an inflated raw index count, and this pattern was trusted uniformly across all other leaf categories on the same platform/template. STRUCTURE: site organizes Home & Food department by room/type (Bedroom, Kitchen, Dining, Bathroom & Laundry, Home Decor, Outdoor & BBQ, etc.), each with its own flat subcategory list (no deeper branching found on any leaf page -- no Rule 0.6 dual-tree case here). SCOPE: extracted from Home Decor (photo/vases/bowls-trays/sculptures-objects/lamps-lighting/mirrors-wall-art/clocks/candle-holders/plants-planters) and Dining (dinnerware/glasses/serveware, filed under Kitchen & Dining per brief). EXCLUDED with reasons: Home Decor -- Throws, Cushions (textiles), Home Fragrance (scented, explicit exclude), Furniture (furniture); Dining -- Cutlery (cutlery), Barware (dominated by shakers/openers/flasks -- bar tools, explicit exclude; a few carafes/decanters present but category as a whole is bar-tools-led so dropped whole rather than padded), Table Linen (textile); Bathroom -- Towels, Bathrobes, Bath Mats (textiles), Laundry (excluded dept), Bathroom Accessories (89 items) DROPPED as a mixed roll-up: title sample dominated by toilet-brush holders, soap/lotion dispensers, tumbler/toothbrush holders, bathroom scales, tile scrubbers, squeegees -- functional/hygiene/plumbing-adjacent per Rule 0.4/0.5, not 'genuinely decorative'; the one mirror spotted in that listing (Hollywood Arch Mirror) is already covered under Mirrors & Wall Art so nothing decorative is lost by dropping it. Bedroom dept: all textile/bedding, nothing decorative, skipped entirely. Kitchen dept (Cookware, Kitchen Appliances, Food Prep, Knives & Chopping Boards, Storage & Organisation, Bakeware, Lunch Boxes): all functional, skipped. Outdoor & BBQ (Gardening, Outdoor Furniture, Outdoor Rugs): no decorative subcategory found, skipped. Books & Stationery: pure books/stationery, no decor items (no bookends etc.), skipped. FACET RE-CUTS excluded per Rule 0.6/naming rule: Designer Decor (/designer/home/decor, numberOfItems=1260), Designer Dining, Designer Bathroom -- confirmed brand-tier facet subsets of the parent decor/dining catalogues (Designer Decor's 1260 is a strict subset of Home Decor's 3615 aggregate), not independent listings. Kids' Dinnerware (/home/dining/dinnerware/kids) is a child slug of Dinnerware and rolls up into the parent's 1013 total -- not counted separately to avoid double-count. Rugs (/home/decor/rugs/outdoor) found referenced from Outdoor page but is a textile category, excluded regardless. No duplicate-company flag applies to S.N. 209 in the brief.
